name: Green Baboon, Defender of the Forest (Retro Formats)
desc: When a Beast-Type monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard, you can pay 1000 Life Points to Special Summon this card from your hand or the Graveyard.

cdb_provenance.detail: type, atk, def, level, race, attribute and setcode are copied from the row for the modern card (46668237) in cards.cdb at the ignis-babelcdb revision pinned in data/sources.json. They are NOT independently checked against a period printing: a stat change between the period card and the modern one would not be reproduced. category (a client search filter, not gameplay) is left 0 rather than copied. ot is 8 (SCOPE_ILLEGAL) as for every historical-implementation row upstream.

modified.summary: no face-up requirement, as the period text has none (a UDE ruling that says otherwise is not shown to have held at the snapshots); the effect description is read from the modern card's strings.

authorship.note: Adapted from Project Ignis's script for the modern card, official/c46668237.lua at the ignis-cardscripts pin, by applying only the period difference the erratum record states (the summary above) and pointing the effect description at the modern card's strings, because this generated row carries none. It is licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later like its upstream (LICENSES/AGPL-3.0-or-later.txt); the rest of this repository stays MIT. Round 031 labelled it original, written without opening any Project Ignis card script; round 031's review measured that version as too close to this upstream file to be independent, and the owner decided on 2026-09-27 that such scripts are credited, labelled derived and kept under the upstream's licence. Round 032 rebased it on the upstream file itself. Round 035 (2026-09-29): the Damage Step flag (EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP) was removed after Konami's errata lists and rulebook were found to forbid Damage Step activation; the script now differs from Ignis's only in dropping the face-up requirement. Superseded modification notice, kept: "no face-up requirement, and activation allowed in the Damage Step (EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP), as the period text has neither restriction" (2026-09-27).

not_reproduced: The script excludes the Damage Step, as the modern card does, because Konami's errata lists (compiled 2009-07-30, 2010-01-05, 2010-11-05) say "You cannot activate the effect of this card during the Damage Step". Not reproduced: the earlier UDE/Konami card FAQ entry that allowed it (2008-12-15), which those lists replace; and where outside the Damage Step a period player could activate it, which is the engine's ordinary timing for an optional "when" trigger.

The record's sources establish that the period text has no face-up requirement on the destroyed Beast. As in the upstream script, the destroyed monster must be a Beast both in the Graveyard and by the engine's record of its race on the field; only a face-down Beast destroyed by a card effect is tested. A UDE ruling (Netrep 2007-09-28; card FAQ 2008-12-15) says a face-down destroyed Beast does not trigger the card; whether it held at the snapshots is not shown, so this difference stays and is on the owner's list.

The period text does not say whether this card being destroyed itself counts as the trigger. As in the upstream script, it is not offered when this card is itself among the cards sent to the Graveyard in that event, even if another Beast was destroyed with it.

As in the upstream script, the trigger carries no EFFECT_FLAG_DELAY, so it follows the engine's rule for an optional "when" trigger and can miss its timing if the destruction is not the last thing to happen (round 031's script used the delayed form). Which the period card followed is not established by the record's sources, and it is not tested.
"You can pay 1000 Life Points to Special Summon" is implemented as a cost paid on activation.
The Special Summon is from the hand or Graveyard into any free Monster Zone in face-up Attack Position; the effect is one trigger for both locations.
The card row's statline is copied from the modern row and not checked against the period printing.

Konami's errata lists say that when several copies are available only 1 may be Special Summoned. One two-copy scenario was run (Dark Hole, two copies in hand): the modern and the generated script each Special Summoned one; the rule is not otherwise tested.

rulings_check.difference: The destroyed Beast need not have been face-up; the modern card requires a face-up Beast.
